tools.name: AggregateResponses
tools.description:
Return aggregate response counts and text-answer distributions for a form.

Samples up to `limit` responses from the first page returned by the Forms
API, which comes back in no guaranteed order. Does not paginate; the counts
and distributions reflect only that sample and can undercount recent activity
on busy forms, which should rely on the response-listing tool's timestamp
filter or the linked response spreadsheet for exhaustive analytics.

parameters.name: form_id
parameters.description: The Google Form ID.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum responses to sample for the summary (1-1000). Summaries reflect only the sampled responses, not the full form. Defaults to 500.

output.description: Get text-answer distributions and rolling-window counts over a sampled set of responses. more_responses_available indicates the form has more responses than were included in the summary.

tools.name: GetFormSummary
tools.description:
Return a concise summary of a Google Form for quick triage and discovery.

The Google Forms API does not expose a total response count and returns
responses in no guaranteed order, so `sampled_response_count`,
`latest_sampled_response_at`, and the 24h/7d counts reflect only the sampled
first page and can undercount recent activity on forms larger than the
sample. For accurate recency or exhaustive analytics, use the response-
listing tool's timestamp filter or the linked response spreadsheet.

parameters.name: form_id
parameters.description: The Google Form ID.

parameters.name: sample_limit
parameters.description: Maximum responses to sample for recent-activity counts (1-200). Defaults to 200.

output.description: Get a quick read on a form for triage: title, structure counts, publish/response-acceptance state, quiz mode, linked-sheet presence, trashed state, and recent-response counts sampled from the first page.

tools.name: ListForms
tools.description:
List Google Forms filtered by a discovery mode such as recent, shared, or in_folder.

Returns results newest-first (by Drive modified time). Each call fetches one
Drive page of up to `limit` forms and returns a `next_page_token` to continue.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Discovery mode. Defaults to recent.

parameters.name: folder_id
parameters.description: Folder ID for in_folder mode. Defaults to empty.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Search query by form title. Defaults to empty.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum results to return in one call (1-50). Defaults to 20.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Continuation token from a previous call's next_page_token. Defaults to an empty string, which returns the first page.

output.description: List forms with mode-aware discovery filters. Each item exposes the Drive file name (`drive_name`), which is the document title set in Drive, not the in-form title set via Forms UI. Fetch the full form to read its actual title. Under the drive.file OAuth scope, results are limited to forms the app created or the user has opened with it. Pass `next_page_token` back as `page_token` for the next page; an empty `next_page_token` means no more results.

tools.name: SetFormSettings
tools.description:
Update form-wide settings (quiz mode, email collection) safely.

Wraps `batchUpdate` + `updateSettings` with a correct `updateMask` built
from the parameters the caller supplied. At least one of `is_quiz` or
`email_collection_type` must be set; otherwise this returns a validation
error so callers never accidentally submit an empty update.

Form-wide settings that are NOT available in Forms API v1 and must be
toggled in the Forms UI (Settings / gear icon):

- "Limit to 1 response"
- "Shuffle question order" per respondent
- Quiz feedback toggles: when to release the grade, whether respondents
  see missed questions, correct answers, or point values. Only `isQuiz`
  is exposed here; per-question `Feedback` + `correctAnswers` +
  `pointValue` still flows through the batch form-update tool.

parameters.name: form_id
parameters.description: The Google Form ID.

parameters.name: is_quiz
parameters.description: Set to true to enable quiz mode, false to disable. Disabling quiz mode deletes all question grading data per the Forms API. Defaults to leaving the current value unchanged.

parameters.name: email_collection_type
parameters.description: Email collection mode: DO_NOT_COLLECT, VERIFIED (Google-account email), or RESPONDER_INPUT (typed by respondent). Defaults to leaving the current value unchanged.

output.description: Update the narrow set of form-wide settings exposed by the Forms API. Sends an explicit updateMask so fields the caller did not touch are preserved. Only the fields supplied here are sent.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: SetPublishSettings
tools.description:
Update a form's publish/response-accepting state.

The Forms API `setPublishSettings` endpoint does not accept an update mask,
so an incomplete body silently unpublishes the form. This wrapper reads the
form's current publish state and merges in only the fields the caller
supplied, so an unset field is preserved rather than reset.

parameters.name: form_id
parameters.description: The Google Form ID.

parameters.name: is_published
parameters.description: Whether the form is published. Providing true publishes the form; providing false unpublishes a live form. Defaults to leaving the current publish state unchanged.

parameters.name: is_accepting_responses
parameters.description: Whether the form accepts new responses. Providing true or false sets that state. A form cannot accept responses while unpublished. Defaults to leaving the current value unchanged.

output.description: Update a form's publish state. Each flag left unset is merged from the form's current state, so a caller can change one field without accidentally toggling the other.

tools.name: UpdateForm
tools.description:
Apply a batch of structural updates to a Google Form.

All structural edits to a form go through this tool. Requests apply
atomically in the given order, so an earlier createItem shifts the indices
that later requests address.

updateItem, updateFormInfo, and updateSettings take an updateMask: only the
named field paths are written, and a field left out of the mask is preserved.
Omitting the mask makes Google overwrite the entire target object.

Forms API v1 limitations to know:
- `questionGroupItem` (grids) has no per-item `required`; mark each
  `rowQuestion` required instead.
- Per-question grading (`pointValue`, `correctAnswers`, `whenRight` /
  `whenWrong` feedback) IS settable here, but the form-wide quiz release
  toggles (when grades are released; whether respondents see missed
  questions, correct answers, or point values) are UI-only.
- "Limit to 1 response" and per-respondent question shuffle are UI-only;
  `choiceQuestion.shuffle` only shuffles options within one question.

Concurrency: pass `required_revision_id` (the revision id from a prior read
of the form) to reject writes that would overwrite concurrent edits. The
returned `revision_id` is the new post-update revision only when
`include_form_in_response=True`; otherwise it is empty and must be re-read
by fetching the form.

parameters.name: form_id
parameters.description: The Google Form ID.

parameters.name: operations
parameters.description: Ordered batchUpdate requests, each object setting exactly one request key. updateItem, updateFormInfo, and updateSettings MUST include an updateMask naming the field paths to change; omitting it makes Google overwrite the entire target object.

parameters.name: required_revision_id
parameters.description: Strict revision precondition. Defaults to empty.

parameters.name: target_revision_id
parameters.description: Transform target revision. Defaults to empty.

parameters.name: include_form_in_response
parameters.description: Include updated form in API response. Defaults to false.

output.description: Apply structural updates to a Google Form. Common recipes below use the exact Forms API v1 request shapes so agents do not have to guess nested field paths or enum names.

summary:
Google Forms toolkit for Arcade enables LLMs to create, read, update, and manage Google Forms and their responses programmatically via the Google Forms and Drive APIs.

## Capabilities

- **Form lifecycle management** — create, copy, rename, trash, restore, and configure form-wide settings (quiz mode, email collection, publish/response-accepting state)
- **Structural editing** — apply atomic batched updates to form items, settings, and metadata with revision-safe concurrency control
- **Response access and analysis** — list, retrieve, and aggregate form responses with timestamp filtering; surface per-question answer distributions from sampled data
- **Discovery and permissions** — list forms by recency, sharing, or folder; inspect and enumerate Drive permissions; generate a Google File Picker URL to resolve access issues
- **Real-time notifications** — create, list, renew, and delete Pub/Sub watches on forms for new responses or schema changes
- **Identity and diagnostics** — retrieve the authenticated user's Google identity (email and display name)

## OAuth

Authentication uses OAuth 2.0 via the Google provider. See the [Arcade Google auth provider docs](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/references/auth-providers/google) for setup details.
